Every Thursday is Open Day
Book a call with our Admissions Office or arrange a private tour to visit our bilingual primary school and nursery at a time that suits you best.Pick the date and time that works for you: we can’t wait to meet you and your family!
Bilingual Nursery for 3-4 years old
Our Nursery caters for children between the ages of 3 and 4 years old. 15 and 30 hours early education funding is available.
Bilingual Primary School
We offer a unique bilingual English/Italian curriculum in a caring and supportive learning environment.
Italian Language courses
Since 2018 the charity that runs our school has also been offering Italian language and culture courses.
We are the only English/Italian school in the UK
A bilingual education can help your child grow to their fullest potential.
SIAL.school is an independent primary school with nursery located in the heart of London, in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, just a short distance from Holland Park. By attending our school, your child will not only learn to speak, read and write two languages, but will also gain valuable knowledge of another culture and way of life, and have wider opportunities when it comes to choosing secondary education.
Why choose us
Are you considering enrolling your child?
Admissions for September 2026 are open for entry into any year group.Applying for a school place can be daunting, so if you are not sure where to start,get in touch and let us guide you through the process.
More about our school
Read more about what makes our bilingual and bi-curricular school unique.
Wraparound care
We believe it is important to support our children and their parents in any way we can and that is why we offer before and after school provision on site at our school. We offer a safe, stimulating and happy environment where children are supervised and engaged in a variety of activities.
Music, Art, Drama, P.E.
At our school, every child has access to high quality music, art and drama lessons, taught by specialist teachers.
Our PE classes strive to give children a lifelong love of being active, while offering the opportunity to take part in a wide range of sports activities which are carried out in a safe and supportive environment.
Learning enrichment
Enrichment activities are designed to give our pupils the opportunity to try new things and learn new skills both inside and outside the classroom.From educational trips to workshops held by visiting experts, from contests and competitions to charity involvement, children benefit from an enhanced curriculum which values and extends their knowledge, experience, interests and competencies.

Our Vision and Values
At SIAL.school, we believe in the importance of giving children the opportunity to be heard as well as getting involved in shaping their future. Our aim is to create a positive and inclusive community within the school that prepares children for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life.
Learning with purpose, growing with confidence
SIAL.school is a vibrant, nurturing educational setting where bilingualism, culture and ambition come together to create something truly special. Here, learning is not only rigorous. It is joyful, purposeful and personal.
We are proud to offer a unique approach that combines the best of both the Italian and British systems.Our community is united by a shared belief in the power of education to broaden horizons and build lasting confidence.
We believe in teamwork, bringing together students, families and our dedicated school staff so that every child is challenged, supported, inspired and, above all, safe. We value high expectations, strong relationships and a clear sense of identity. Our students leave us not only well-prepared for academic success, but also equipped with empathy, resilience, honesty and self-awareness to navigate the world with confidence.
B.R.A.I.N.S.: our curriculum, our values
Our curriculum reflects this vision. We call it BRAINS:
B – Bilingual and Bi-curricularLearning unfolds in both English and Italian daily, combining two rigorous curricula to develop deep thinking skills, cognitive flexibility and cultural fluency.
R- Rooted in CultureOur students grow up with a strong sense of belonging, respect for diverse perspectives and traditions, and a commitment to becoming responsible global citizens.
A – Ambition-DrivenOur approach is purposeful and well-structured. We encourage children to set high goals, and we guide them every step of the way.
I – Inclusive CommunityWe nurture respectful and kind individuals, and foster a community where everyone feels valued and respected.
N – Nurturing ConfidenceOur small classes enable us to truly get to know each child. We cultivate independence, curiosity, courage and creativity from the earliest years.
S – Strong Identity and Global OutlookOur students are grounded in who they are and prepared to contribute thoughtfully and openly to the wider world.
> Read more about our bilingual curriculum
What OFSTED said about us
> OFSTED inspection – May 2026
We warmly invite you to visit us and see how our unique approach comes to life every day: book your school tour, we’d love to welcome you!
Our school’s weekly values
At our school, we believe that a strong foundation of core values is essential to shaping a nurturing and effective learning environment. Our weekly values are carefully designed to inspire and cultivate these principles, which are at the heart of everything we do. These values are not just taught—they are lived. Our staff model them daily, ensuring that children experience and embrace them throughout their learning journey.
Respect
At SIAL school we are respectful by speaking in turns, by sharing toys and resources, by lining up nicely, by speaking to each other with kindness, and by having manners.
Kindness
At SIAL school we are kind by taking care of each other’s safety and emotions, by making sure that our words don’t hurt others, by looking after all living creatures, and by seeking to understand before making judgments.
Honesty
At SIAL school we are honest by telling the truth even when it is hard to say it and by giving our opinion with kindness and respect. Being honest can be difficult because it takes great courage and strength. When you are honest you are also courageous.
Creativity
At SIAL school we are creative by participating in activities with imagination and enthusiasm, by solving problems with an open mind, and by expressing our personality through art, writing, drama and music.
Resilience
At SIAL school we are resilient by having an open mind about mistakes, by participating in activities even when we think it’s too hard, by not being discouraged if something seems difficult and by staying positive whenever we feel challenged.
Responsibility
At SIAL school we are responsible by looking after each other and the environment, by following the teachers’ instructions, by behaving properly in school, by being reliable during a school trip, and by completing the homework on time.
Courage
At SIAL school we are courageous by taking risks when trying new things and activities. We are not afraid of making mistakes.
Independence
At SIAL School, we are independent by self-regulating our behaviour, take initiative in our learning, and approach challenges with a positive, solution-focused mindset.
Come and see how our values shape the way we learn.
Step into our classrooms, meet our community, and experience the joy of learning at SIAL.school – join us on an Open Day or book a private school tour at your convenience.> Book a school tour
Equality, diversity and inclusion
The principles of Equality and Diversity are essential to our work.
At SIAL.school we actively work to ensure that all children and adults are given every opportunity to achieve, to recognise their own worth and to play an important part in our community.
A key part of our plan for education is to ensure children become valuable and fully rounded members of society who treat others with respect and tolerance, regardless of their background.
Read more about our Gold Equalities Award
Our History
SIAL.school began as a project in 2004, when a group of Italian citizens reached out to the large community of Italians living in London to gauge interest in setting up an Italian school.
2007Our Charity was set up
In July 2007 the charity which to this day manages the school (SIAL.charity, La Scuola Italiana a Londra, Reg. Charity no. 1119966), was set up and started raising funds to open the school.
2010Our school opened its doors
The School opened the nursery on the 8th of September 2010. Since then, the Board of Trustees has managed the business side of the school and supported its continual development through fundraising campaigns and various activities.
2012Our first Y1 class
The Primary School opened on 11th September 2012 with the Y1 class. Today the school has completed the primary cycle and educates children from the age of 3 to 11.
2016Our new building
The school widens and rents a new building, thanks to the support of Ambassador Pasquale Q. Terracciano.
Read more about our school's history on SIAL.charity's website.
2023A secondary school
Together with a group of Italian parents living in London, we are currently exploring the idea of widening our educational offer by opening a fully bilingual and bi-curricular secondary school.Register to get further updates.
SIAL.school’s annual accounts are available online on the Charity Commission for England and Wales’ website. Go to the Charity Commission’s website
Promoting the Italian language and culture
Since its foundation in 2007, SIAL.charity has worked to promote the knowledge and support the understanding of the Italian language and culture in the UK, not only through the provision of a bilingual English-Italian education at SIAL.school, but also through the offering of courses, clubs and events open to the general public, under the brand SIAL.courses.

Welcome to our bilingual school
SIAL.school is the only English/Italian bilingual and bi-curricular primary school with nursery in the UK.
Children from 3 to 11 benefit from tailored lesson plans in a safe and nurturing learning environment, in the heart of London.Our independent school and nursery are based in West London, Holland Park (W11 4UH).
Our Unicity
Letter from our Headteacher
Vision and Values
Your child is unique, so is our school.
We want to create a safe and nurturing learning environment where children are encouraged to fulfill their personal and academic potential. We aim to inspire a passion for knowledge as well as stimulating the personal interests and abilities of each student.
Our bilingual school is proudly part of the Italian network of educational institutions in the world (Sistema della Formazione Italiana nel Mondo).State-authorized schools (“scuole paritarie”) are schools managed by entities other than the State, which undertake to help achieve the educational purposes assigned to them by the Italian Constitution and are recognised by the State as having the same status as state schools. There are 46 Italian state-authorized private schools abroad. Found on all continents, they engage around 20,000 pupils and help promote the Italian language and culture according to foreign policy guidelines.
Financial transparencyWe are delighted to inform you that the allocation plan for the funding available for Capitolo 2619, Management Plan 1 (grant funds for State-authorized schools, “scuole paritarie”) for the financial year 2025 has been approved by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. SIAL received €59.549,00.
SIAL.school’s annual accounts are available online on the Charity Commission for England and Wales’ website. Go to the Charity Commission’s website

Music, Art, Drama and P.E.
At SIAL.school Music, Art, Drama and Physical Education form an integral part of the school curriculum and are taught by specialist teachers both in Italian and English throughout the academic years.
Music
Music plays a huge part in our school life and is taught by a specialist teacher as a class subject to every child from Nursery. Through musical activities, the children develop the confidence to express their creativity, empathy and personality. Classroom activities focus on performing, listening and learning about the key elements of music.
All the children are encouraged to explore and expand their abilities in the vocal, rhythmic and instrumental areas and to learn to express and develop their ideas using music as much as they do drawing or movement.
From Year 1 we also offer individual tuition on a variety of instruments, including piano, violin, recorder, flute, guitar and ukulele.
Art
Children are exposed to a wide variety of materials and techniques in order to give them the opportunity to discover their own potential. Projects are structured to allow children of varying abilities to be confident and achieve success.The main objectives are for the children to acquire practical skills, develop a love of creating and to learn to express their own creativity and individuality.Our pupils have access to a beautiful art classroom, a dedicated space which allows for plenty of creativity and messy, expressive art!
Drama
Our specialist drama teacher works closely with individual class teachers to support, complement and extend the core curriculum.Creative movement, speaking skills and improvisation, as well as a sense of audience and timing, are all developed with increasing degrees of experimentation and expected versatility as the children work their way through the school.The emphasis here is on enjoyment, teamwork and developing skills that provide fulfillment, promote self-confidence and discipline and enrich each child’s appreciation for the magic and potential of their imaginations.Every year the children are provided with several opportunities to exhibit their understanding and skills during more formal performances, not least during a whole school production; which brings together a broad range of learning areas and requirements from Dance, Art and Design to English, Italian, History, Geography and others, depending on the themes of the production.
P.E.
We seek to develop each child’s Physical Literacy; namely the techniques, knowledge, self-awareness and instincts which will best aid the enjoyment, fluency, and efficiency with which they contribute to a wide variety of sporting experiences, regardless of the level of competition.This ethos is mainly pursued via a series of small and large group games, exercises and opportunities which, with evolving variations in rules and expectations, require the children to consistently adapt their approach – increasing the capability and flexibility of their responses – in order to succeed.We provide two hours of high quality PE and sport per week: one session is normally carried out at school, the other is carried out outdoors at the local park, to allow children to run around a larger open space and unwind in the fresh-air.Swimming classes are arranged for students from Y1-Y6.
Our bilingual curriculum
At SIAL.school we teach a completely bilingual, bi-cultural and bi-curricular education, which integrates the Italian Curriculum with the best of the British education system.
This approach enables us to offer the best of both systems in terms of content, teaching methods and skills acquired by the children and enables our pupils to move freely into either the Italian or the British school system or get into international schools.

pageCache.text:
Musica, Arte, Recitazione ed Educazione Motoria
Alla SIAL.school Musica, Arte, Recitazione ed Educazione Motoria sono parte integrante del curriculum scolastico e sono insegnate da insegnanti specialisti in italiano e in inglese durante tutto il percorso scolastico, dalla scuola dell’infanzia fino a Y6, ultimo anno della scuola primaria.
Musica
L’educazione musicale riveste un ruolo estremamente importante nella nostra scuola e fa parte del programma didattico fin dalla Nursery.
Attraverso l’attività musicale, i bambini sviluppano fiducia nell’esprimere la loro creatività, empatia e personalità.
Le attività di classe puntano sull’esecuzione, l’ascolto e l’apprendimento degli elementi fondamentali della musica. Tutti i bambini vengono incoraggiati ad esplorare ed espandere le loro capacità vocali, ritmiche e strumentali e ad imparare a esprimere e sviluppare le loro idee utilizzando la musica esattamente come fanno con il disegno o il movimento.
A partire da Y1 offriamo lezioni individuali di diversi strumenti, tra cui piano. violino, fluato, chitarra e ukulele.
Arte
I bambini lavorano con una grande varietà di materiali e tecniche, al fine di dare ad ognuno la possibilità di scoprire le proprie potenzialità.
I progetti vengono strutturati in modo da permettere a bambini di abilità diverse di lavorare con serenità per il raggiungimento degli obiettivi formativi.
L’obiettivo principale è quello di aiutare i bambini ad acquisire competenze pratiche, sviluppare la passione per la creazione e imparare a esprimere la propria creatività e individualità.
Nell’aula di arte nostri allievi trovano spazio dedicato che permette di dare libero sfogo alla creatività e cimentarsi anche con le forme d’arte più espressive senza preoccuparsi di sporcare!
Recitazione
L’insegnante specialista di recitazione lavora a stretto contatto con gli insegnanti di ogni classe per supportare, completare e arricchire il programma principale.
Movimento creativo, doti oratorie, improvvisazione, capacità di affrontare un pubblico e senso del tempo sono tutte abilità che vengono affinate durante il percorso scolastico, sperimentando e mettendo alla prova la propria versatilità.
L’enfasi resta sempre sul divertimento, il lavoro di squadra e lo sviluppo di competenze che promuovano la fiducia in se stessi, la disciplina e un senso di realizzazione, mentre i bambini imparano ad apprezzare e sfruttare il potenziale della loro immaginazione.
Ogni anno i bambini hanno diverse opportunità di esibirsi e mettere in scena quanto appreso, in occasioni più o meno strutturate, fino alla produzione di uno spettacolo che coinvolge l’intera scuola.
La produzione di questo spettacolo prevede un approccio interdisciplinare che coniuga materie e aree di apprendimento diverse, come inglese, italiano, storia, geografia, a seconda del tema dello spettacolo stesso.
Educazione motoria
Miriamo a sviluppare in ogni bambino la cosiddetta Alfabetizzazione Fisica, ossia le tecniche, la conoscenza, la consapevolezza di sé e gli istinti che concorrono a sviluppare la fluidità, la riuscita e il divertimento con cui i bambini partecipano alle varie esperienze sportive, indipendentemente dal livello di agonismo richiesto.
Lavoriamo principalmente attraverso una serie di giochi di gruppo, piccoli e grandi, ed esercizi che, con regole e aspettative sempre più complesse, richiedono ai bambini di adeguare costantemente il loro approccio, aumentando via via la capacità e la flessibilità delle loro risposte.
Offiramo due ore di educazione motoria e sport a settimana: una sessione avviene normalmente all’interno della scuola, l’altra all’esterno, nel parco vicino alla scuola, per dare ai bambini la possibilità di correre in ampi spazi e rilassarsi all’aria aperta.
Da Y1 a Y6 i bambini frequentano anche lezioni di nuoto.
Due lingue per le materie
Alla SIAL.school offriamo un’istruzione completamente bilingue, bi-culturale e bi-curricolare, che integra il programma didattico italiano con il meglio del sistema educativo inglese. Questo approccio ci permette di offrire il meglio di entrambi i sistemi scolastici in termini di contenuti, approcci didattici e competenze acquisite dai bambini, che sono in grado di spostarsi facilmente dal sistema scolastico italiano a quello inglese (e viceversa) o proseguire i propri studi in una scuola internazionale
Privacy Overview
Italiano

Our Partners
At SIAL.school we recognise the importance of a trusted network and we are proud to have built and developed several collaborations with public, private and community partners over the years.
The Italian Institutions
The main objective of SIAL.school is to create an Italian school which is fully integrated with the British context in which it operates. We work in partnership with all the Italian institutions in London, which also actively participate in our school life and development, from H.E. the Italian Ambassador, who is one of the Patrons of the Charity that runs the school, to the Italian Cultural Institute and the Consulate General of Italy, and especially its Educational Department, who support us in the implementation of the Italian side of our curriculum.
Our local community
Being a bi-lingual, bi-curricular school, it is fundamental for us to build a positive relationship with our local community to create a bridge between the Italian community and the context within which we live and operate.
We work very closely with the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, which helps to foster the development of our school and supports us in the implementation of the English side of our curriculum through the Local Education Authority.
We also involve the local community in our school life, by organising outings to local facilities, i.e. the Fire Station, or by inviting key people of the local community, i.e. police officers, the Mayor of the Council and our local MP to visit the school to talk to the children.
SIAL.school is also proud to engage and work in partnership with our friends and partners who share our vision of promoting the Italian language and culture in the UK:
Il Circolo
Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Londra
Our school networks
We are delighted to share with you that our bilingual school is part of multiple school networks worldwide promoting the dissemination of good practice and supporting innovation.
We are delighted to announce that we are members of the Bilingual Education Alliance (BEA), an alliance of leaders of bilingual schools as well as academics, policy makers, parents and others who share our vision of supporting and promoting the growing movement of bilingual schools in England.
Our bilingual school is proudly part of the Italian network of educational institutions in the world (Sistema della Formazione Italiana nel Mondo).State-authorized schools (“scuole paritarie”) are schools managed by entities other than the State, which undertake to help achieve the educational purposes assigned to them by the Italian Constitution and are recognised by the State as having the same status as state schools. There are 43 Italian state-authorized private schools abroad. Found on all continents, they engage more than 16,000 pupils and help promote the Italian language and culture according to foreign policy guidelines.
The school has also been a member of the UNESCO Associated Schools Network since the academic year 2017/2018. The UNESCO Associated Schools is a global network of schools which work in support of international understanding, peace, intercultural dialogue, sustainable development and quality education in practice. It links 11,500 educational institutions in 182 countries with a common goal: to build the defences of peace in the minds of children and young people. The UNESCO Associated Schools Network is recognized as an effective tool for reaching target 4.7 on Global Citizenship Education (GCED) and Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) of Sustainable Development Goal 4 – Education 2030.
Find out more about our school: discover our bilingual curriculum, our vision and values, the awards and achievements we have gained over time.
We are committed to provide parents and carers with useful and practical advice, so don’t hesitate to get in touch with our School Office: they will be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Board of Governors
SIAL.school is managed by SIAL.charity (La Scuola Italiana a Londra) which is a Company limited by guarantee [No 6046404] and a registered charity [No 1119966]. The Board of Governors of SIAL.school is composed of people with professional experience in various fields, from teaching to finance, from law to public relations, who volunteer for the school. They are all connected by the strong belief that the Italian language and its culture are worth keeping alive and teaching, not only to Italians but to anyone else who recognises their value.
The Board manages the business side of the school, whilst the day to day operations are superbly managed by our Headteacher.
Our Board
Alberto Pravettoni - Chair of the Board
Alberto is the Chair of Board. He has been involved in the project since November 2005, and his main focus has been on the financial business planning. He graduated in Business Administration at Bocconi University in Milan and attended a post graduate program on Management in Global Enterprises at the American School of International Management (Phoenix, AZ). In 2004, he completed a “Nonprofit Leadership Program” at Harvard University, specifically designed for Trustees. Alberto worked for 13 years as a Managing Director at Goldman Sachs, where he was the Global Head of Fixed Income Operations. Most recently, he was a Managing Director and member of the Executive Committee at LCH.Clearnet. Between 2003 and 2007, he sat on the Board of Trustees of “La Scuola d’Italia G. Marconi” in New York.
Rossana Bottino
Rossana is one of our teaching assistants and is the teachers’ representative on our Board. Rossana graduated in Lingue e Letterature Moderne at the Istituto Universitario di Lingue Moderne in Milan. She has a Higher Level Teaching Assistant Level 4 certificate, a Level 5 TEFL certificate and a certificate in Supporting Learners with Dyslexia and SpLD. She has experience in teaching Italian, English, French and Spanish as foreign languages.
Ada Cerne
Ada joined the Board of Trustees in 2019 and is primarily involved with the financial business planning of the Charity. Since 2014, Ada has worked at Edmond de Rothschild Asset Management (UK), where she is Managing Director and Head of Digital Infrastructure within their Infrastructure and Structured Finance department. She began her career in the Investment Banking Division of BZW / Barclays Capital in the late Nineties and later moved to the Structured Finance Department at WestLB AG where she spent 14 years primarily in the telecoms and acquisition finance teams. Whilst a senior originator at WestLB, she also acted as country manager for Sub-Saharan Africa. Ada obtained an IB Diploma from the United World College of South East Asia (Singapore). She holds a BA in Economics and an MSc in Development Economics from The School of Oriental and African Studies, London University. She is a CFA Charterholder.
Stefano Donati
Stefano Donati is Managing Director at BlackRock, where he oversee the European investment portfolio for a handful of global multi-asset funds. Prior to joining BlackRock in 2008, Stefano has worked in several investment roles at Goldman Sachs. Stefano graduated in 2001 from Università Bocconi. He is actively involved, with past or current roles, in several social and cultural activities, such as Bocconi Alumni in London; Business Club Italia; Club Torino; Rotary Club of the City and Shoreditch, SIAL Charity - La Scuola Italiana a Londra. Stefano is Cavaliere O.M.S.I.
Christian Iachini
Christian joined the Board of Trustees in October 2017 with the mandate to support the communication and marketing activities of the charity. He has nearly 20 years of experience in digital marketing, having led digital marketing departments in large multinationals. He also holds two Master’s Degrees: one in International Management and Business Administration from Copenhagen Business School and the other in Corporate Communication from the University of Trieste. Christian has 2 trilingual children, one of whom attended SIAL.school.
Ernestina Meloni
Ernestina joined the project in January 2006 and was mainly involved in the coordination of the bilingual aspect of the curriculum. She graduated in Modern Languages at Cagliari University and completed a Master’s Degree in Applied Linguistics at Birkbeck College, University of London. Ernestina has been teaching Italian in the UK for the past forty years in Oxford and London. At present she is a teacher and coordinator of the Italian Department at the Lycée Français Charles de Gaulle in London. She has been working for British and International organizations as a trainer and adviser promoting excellence in language education. She also worked as language adviser for the BBC in the production of various children’s programmes. In 2004 Ernestina won the European Language Award, an Italian Embassy Award for teaching languages through movement and dance and was knighted by the Italian Government as a “Cavaliere all’Ordine del Merito della Repubblica Italiana”. In 2005 she received an award from Chicago University for Best Teaching Practice. Ernestina has been working for various examination boards as Moderator and Principal. She has published books to teach Italian for National British Exams (GCSE and A Level) and she is still publishing articles and educational material on bilingual education and language teaching. She is involved in different EU projects promoting inclusion, dialogue and respect of cultural diversity.
Francesca Nelson-Smith
Founder of the project la Scuola Italiana a Londra, Francesca devoted her spare time to the idea of opening an Italian school since she moved back to London in 1997. Finally in 2004, with the help of Emanuela Federspil and the support of the “Italians of London” organisation, she created the commission “A school for the Italians” with a team of volunteers to work on the project. Francesca succeeded Emanuela as Chair of the Board of Governors in 2011 and maintained the role until August 2017. She remains on the board as Head of Marketing and PR. Francesca graduated in Philosophy and Modern Languages (French) at Oxford University and started her career as a bi-lingual magazine and book producer in London. Subsequently she specialised in the production of promotional events for the SMH- Swatch Group in Milan. Back in London since 1997, she has worked on a number of charities and business projects. On the 10th of March 2016 the Italian Ambassador Pasquale Terracciano awarded Francesca the honour of “Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Stella d’Italia” for her contribution to the promotion of Italian education and culture in the United Kingdom. Francesca has been a member of the board of St Francis of Assisi Primary school since February 2015 and Vice-Chair of the board since September 2019.
Domenic Pini
Domenic joined the team in 2010 to help with legal advice and fundraising. Domenic was educated St George’s College Weybridge, Surrey and Cambridge University. After many years working for a number of practices in London, he is now a Partner of Pini Franco LLP. Domenic was Chairman of the British Italian Law Association 1984 to 1996 and former President of the City of London Rotary Club and a Council Member of Business Club Italia as well as Freeman of the City of London. Awarded by the President of the Italian Republic on 28 12 2015 “Ufficiale Ordine della Stella D’Italia”. Member of the International Court of Appeal of the UIM (Union Internationale Motoautique) for the four-year terms 2019-2023.
Michaela Rees Jones
Michaela joined the board in 2014. Following a degree in Modern Languages she pursued a professional career in International Education in Europe and the USA. Early work in teaching was followed by several years working in marketing, publishing and recruitment for Interstudy Inc and EF. More recently she has focussed on volunteering and fundraising for a number of local good causes. Through the English Speaking Union Michaela has helped with the EAL programme at a primary school in North Kensington, is a former Vice-Chair of The Second Half Foundation, sits on the board of the charity Action Against Cancer and is a member of the Witness Service team at the Central Criminal Court.
Ines Saltalamacchia
Ines Saltalamacchia has been involved in the project La Scuola Italiana a Londra since March 2006 — first as a Trustee and, following the opening of the School, as part of its management team for the first few years and as Headteacher from January 2015 until August 2024. During this time, she contributed to the development of SIAL.school’s distinctive bilingual and bi-curricular teaching programme. She holds a degree in Philosophy from the Università degli Studi di Milano, where she also completed an MSc in Information and Communication Technology for Human Sciences. From 2001 to 2004, Ines worked as a researcher at the Università degli Studi di Milano and King’s College London, earning a PhD in Logic. Ines served as a Governor at Salusbury Primary School for five years and is actively involved with several charities in developing countries, supporting teacher training, curriculum design, and school-wide initiatives aimed at improving educational quality.
The Board of Trustees thanks its first Chair Emanuela Federspil for enabling the opening of SIAL.school through her marketing efforts and commitment to the cause and is grateful to its former board member and Chair Raffaella Celia for her leadership, legal acumen and selfless commitment which have been invaluable to the school and our charity over the years.

Wraparound Care
At SIAL.school we believe it is important to support our children and their parents in any way we can and that is why we offer wraparound childcare on site.
Before-school Provision
We provide a before school provision from 8:00 AM.
From 8:00 AM parents/carers are able to come into the school and leave the children in the library, where members of our staff will supervise them until 8:20 AM when the children will be escorted to their classrooms.
Our Before-school Provision is free of charge and open to all children who attend the school from Nursery to Year 6.
Extended Hours Provision
Our Extended Hours Provision aims to support working parents and carers by providing after-school supervision for children until 6:00 PM.
This is different from our after-school clubs which are meant to extend the main curriculum and develop individual talents and interests, and which are offered at the end of the school day from Monday to Thursday.
Families who apply for the Extended Hours Provision have the possibility to leave their children in school every day, Monday to Friday, with members of our staff supervising them until 6:00PM. Children attending an after-school club can still benefit from the Extended Hours Provision after their chosen club ends and spend more time with their friends until pick-up time.
All the children will have the opportunity to mix with others from all year groups in a stimulating and happy environment, which promotes their learning and development.
Our Extended Hours Provision caters for all children from Nursery to Year 6 who attend the school and operates in term time only.
The cost of the service will be as follows:– EYFS (from 3:15 to 6pm): £80 per week or £2,574.00 for the full year; term booking are also available– KS1&KS2 (from 3:30/4:00 to 6pm): £54 per week or £1,716.00 for the full year; term booking are also available
To request a place or if you have any questions, please feel free to contact us at 020 7603 5353 or email the team at finance@sial.school.Extended Hours Provision fees will be invoiced before the beginning of the term.
Ad Hoc sessions may be offered at the price of £20 per hour, if there is availability of places. Ad Hoc sessions must be booked on SignUp.
After-school Clubs
At SIAL.school children also have the option of attending a range of after-school clubs which include traditional sport and music clubs, as well as many other extra-curricular activities.

Parent Association
The school is one of the first places where children genuinely experience a sense of community. It is therefore essential that the school acts as a meeting place, promoting a sense of belonging and participation within the school itself and in connection with the families and the local area.
At SIAL.school the cooperation between school and family is the pivot around which all revolves.
Only through a close collaboration can we best understand each child’s individuality and specific needs so as to most efficiently support their learning.For this reason we have an Open Door policy for our parents /carers and they are very welcome to come in to discuss any suggestions, questions or concerns with the school staff.
Our Parent Association plays a vital role in school life.
Our Parent Association (PA) supports the school with proposals, ideas, fundraisers and projects to improve its services and to support educational activities.
It meets periodically, with or without school staff (as needed), to discuss any concerns, make suggestions and implement initiatives in order to improve the services of the school and to consistently support it.
The PA promotes the dialogue between school staff and our pupils’ families, but also provides opportunities for social interaction and communication outside the school, involving prospective parents and the wider Italian/British community.
The Association is a not-for-profit organisation; the chair, secretary and treasurer are elected annually.All parents can enrol and are invited to get involved.
To register or for information, please contact the Parent Association by writing to sial.pa@sial.school.For further details download the Parent Association Constitution.
Our Parent Association is working very hard to promote initiatives and events open to the public, supporting our mission and making the school known across the Italian and international families in London. If you would like to know more or attend the upcoming events, do not hesitate to drop them an email.

Pastoral Care
We are a listening school and central to our pastoral care policy is the belief that all children have the right to start and end the day in a happy frame of mind.
You can read our Pastoral Care Code of Practice here.
Rules are kept to a minimum and aim to ensure the safety and happiness of the children while they are in school.
We want our school to be a safe and trusting environment where children are encouraged and inspired to become confident, fulfilled and resilient individuals.
Safeguarding
All agencies involved in the care of minors have as their ultimate aim the welfare of children in their care and this is also the priority for all the people working in the school.
We expect all staff, governors, volunteers and visitors to share this commitment to safeguarding our pupils.
We listen actively to our pupils, parents and staff and take seriously what they tell us. No concern is too small and all school staff are trained in Child Protection. Children are made aware that they can talk to any adult if they have any concerns.
To read our regulation on the Protection of Minors click here.
Our doors are always open
You’re welcome to come and visit our school and talk to the staff: book a call or schedule an appointment at your convenience.In the meantime find out more about our fees and admissions process.

After-school Clubs
At SIAL.school we pride ourselves on providing a broad range of opportunities that aid children’s physical and emotional development.
From yoga, to ballet, from puppetry to video-making, from football to cooking, our after-school clubs provide a safe and supportive environment where children can let off steam, improve their confidence and develop good teamwork skills.
Clubs in Italian and English
By offering clubs in both languages (English and Italian) we offer an additional opportunity for our pupils to continue their bilingual and bi-cultural journey even outside of standard school hours.
Clubs are available to all ages from Nursery through to Year 6, with registration at the beginning of each term.
The average fee is usually £250 per term per club.
Places are limited, so do please get in touch with the School Office to find out more.

Our bilingual curriculum
Your child will learn not only to speak but to read and write in both languages, gain valuable knowledge of both cultures and ways of life, and have broader opportunities when it comes to choosing Secondary level education.
A bilingual and bi-curricular education
Our Nursery (EYFS) and Primary School (KS1 & KS2) have a completely bilingual and bicultural curriculum in which the standards set by the Italian Ministry of Education are integrated and complemented by the EYFS Framework and National English Curriculum.
This approach enables us to offer the best of both systems in terms of content, teaching methods and skills acquired by the children and enables our pupils to move freely into either the Italian or the British school system or get into international schools.
For Early Years
Our curriculum builds upon a balance between activities led by our teachers and by the interests of our children who are encouraged to actively influence the course and format of their learning.
Besides the projects which form the Essential Curriculum (the Body, Colours, Shapes, Problem Solving, Reasoning and Numeracy, Introduction to Writing and Reading, Road Safety and so on) every year the school develops specific projects which arise within the class groups, such as: Cooking, Gardening, Recycling, Creativity, The Library, The Universe, are examples covered in the past few years.
Find out more about our bilingual nursery
For Years 1 to 6
Pupils are taught Italian, English, Maths, Science, French, History, Geography, Religious Studies, ICT, Sport, Art, Music and Drama throughout the school.
Personal, Social, Health Education, Citizenship and Philosophy for Children also form an integral part of the general curriculum.
Subjects such as P.E., Art, Drama and Music are taught by specialist teachers.
Extra-Curricular Activities
We complement our bilingual curriculum with a wide and varied programme of extra-curricular activities. We ensure that all of our pupils find something they love and have the opportunity to unwind after a busy day at school and pursue their interests and passions.
A child-centred approach
We prioritise the children’s individual needs and abilities above the traditional expectations for their age. Our educational philosophy and approach are strongly focused on each child’s personal development.
Come and see what makes our school unique
You are welcome to come and visit our Bilingual English/Italian Nursery and Primary School or talk to the Headteacher.
Call us on 020 7603 5353 or fill out the form to book a private tour.

Together with a group of Italian parents living in London, we are currently exploring the idea of widening our educational offer by opening a fully bilingual and bi-curricular secondary school.
To explore the needs and expectations of families who may be interested in this, we circulated an online survey within the Italian community in London and collected more than 500 responses over the summer 2022.
What’s next?
Having analysed all the data collected, we are now working on the business plan while reaching out to the Italian government and institutions to seek their support for this ambitious project.
Keep in touch
If you like the idea of a bilingual English/Italian secondary school and would like to receive further updates on this project, please enter your email address below and we will share relevant news when available.
Should you have any questions, please email us on secondary@sial.school.

Bursaries
The mission of SIAL.school is to offer our unique bilingual and bi-curricular education to all children, regardless of their social and economic background, so we have set up an effective means-tested bursary scheme for all year groups.
A bursary can cover any proportion of the costs of fees up to 100% for those who are eligible.
We judge each application carefully, considering the income and assets of the family.
How to apply for a bursary
To apply for a bursary, you’ll need to prove your financial need.
As well as providing evidence of your income, you may have to give details of your assets, other dependent family members, and even your spending habits, such as holidays.
We review bursaries annually, but these will be continued at the same level if there are no material changes in financial circumstances. If there are changes in circumstances, bursary awards may be varied upwards or downwards.
To apply for a bursary simply contact our Admissions Office at admissions@sial.school or 020 7603 5353.
Find out more about our Admissions Process and our fees.

The admission procedure at SIAL.school is non-selective. Places are allocated prioritising siblings and in order of declaration of interest. All applications will be acknowledged. Once the registration form and registration fee have been received, Parents/Carers will be informed whether their registration has been accepted and the child will be placed on our registration list in the relevant academic year and class.
If you are applying for a place for September 2027, once the registration form and registration fee have been received, you will be informed whether the registration has been accepted and your child will be placed on our registration list in the relevant academic year and class.
Application deadline for the school year 2027-2028 is December 2026, when formal offer letters and relevant forms are sent to those who are on our registration list.
Note: Few places available for admissions in September 2026If you are applying for a place for the school year 2026-2027, our Admissions Office will contact you after you register to send a formal offer letter and the relevant forms, subject to availability in your year group of interest.
If you are applying for a place for a later school year, please note that our Admissions Office will be in touch in due course.
Places are normally offered at the beginning of the December before entry.
Please refer to our Admission Process for further information.

pageCache.text:
Get to know our bilingual school
SIAL.school is the only school in the UK to teach all subjects in English and Italian, from Nursery to Y6.Located in West London, a few steps from Holland Park, the school welcomes children aged 3-11.
Every Thursday is Open Day
We know that every family has different needs, circumstances and timelines.That’s why we believe you shouldn’t have to wait for a specific time of year to discover our school.
Throughout the school year, we welcome prospective families every Thursday morning for a personalised visit, giving you the opportunity to explore our school, meet our team and get a feel for our community.
And if you’re unable to visit us in person, every Thursday afternoon our Admissions Office is available for individual calls, so you can speak to our team and find out more about SIAL from wherever you are.
We welcome children aged 3 to 11, and admissions are open now.
Places for September 2027 will be allocated soon, so we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible to secure a place. We are also accepting applications for the 2028–2029 academic year.
There may also be places available during the current school year. If you are considering enrolling your child, our Admissions Office is available throughout the year to answer your questions and guide you through the process.
Book a call or a private tourand meet our Headteacher and staff.
Choose the option which suits you best and reserve your spot. We very much look forward to meeting you!

A new school year, some exciting news
Winter Open Day: visit our bilingual school this January
A new school year, some exciting news
Winter Open Day: visit our bilingual school this January
You are all invited to visit our bilingual primary school and nursery: our doors will be open on Wednesday 22nd October 2025, from 10:00 to 11:30 AM.
An Open Day is an important opportunity for prospective parents to see for themselves what life at our bilingual school looks like. The purpose of this event is to familiarise you with our bilingual school, provide you with an insight into our daily life and share with you our commitment to recognise each child as an individual.
It will be possible to visit the school during class time, which will give you the opportunity of really seeing the school in action. By observing our everyday activities you will be able to get a rounded view of the school and our special teaching approach, while taking a peek at classrooms and outdoor area.
Agenda 10:00 Welcome 10:15 Presentation 10:45 School Tour 11:15 Q&A
We can’t wait to tell you and show you what an amazing place our bilingual school is!
